cards.summary: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】AutoSynthData: Generating Training Data for Enterprise Agents
fulltext: What makes a useful agentic task? System specification Agent-facing task Verifier Overview From model failures to a curriculum Generating and scaling tasks Target Multiply Implementation details High-quality synthetic data needs more than generation Sample-level verification and repair Batch-level review Moving the training frontier EnterpriseOps Gym experiments Hybrid Hybrid results ITSM Closing the loop

Enterprises need agents that work well in their own environments. The work they ask these agents to do is shaped by the systems they use, the rules they follow, and the state of their data. A model may be broadly capable and still struggle with a particular environment: a workflow it handles poorly, a combination of tools it misuses, or a constraint it fails to respect. Those are the weaknesses an enterprise needs to improve.

The difficulty is turning those weaknesses into training data. An individual failure tells us something, but training a model requires many new tasks that exercise the same capability in different situations. Those tasks must also be possible to complete in the environment, resemble work someone would actually request, and have a reliable way to check whether the agent succeeded.

At ServiceNow CoreAI, we built AutoSynthData to turn those capability gaps into training data. It uses a target model’s failures and a stronger teacher’s successes to decide what the model should learn next, then generates and validates new tasks that exercise those capabilities. As the model improves, the curriculum shifts toward what it still finds difficult. We illustrate the pipeline with EnterpriseOps Gym (Malay et al., 2026), using the released dataset. We begin by describing the environment an agent operates in and what makes a task useful for training.
An agentic environment defines the world in which an agent operates: the state it can observe and modify, the tools and APIs it can invoke, and the state transitions produced by its actions.
A task is instantiated within this environment. We use the following abstraction:

The system specification defines the constraints under which the agent operates, including system instructions, environment policies, and, when applicable, task-specific initialization such as a seeded database state or a set of knowledge articles.

The specification must be compatible with the environment’s tools, state, and supported actions. Its instructions should be clear and avoid arbitrary constraints introduced solely to manufacture difficulty.
The user prompt specifies what the user wants the agent to accomplish, together with any user-level constraints. A generated task should satisfy three properties.

Feasibility. There should exist at least one trajectory in the current environment that satisfies the user prompt while respecting the system specification. This rules out tasks that depend on unavailable tools, inaccessible knowledge, impossible state transitions, or actions prohibited by policy.

Realism. The user prompt should resemble something a user would plausibly ask in the target environment. The space of executable behaviors is usually much larger than the space of realistic workflows.

Difficulty. For training, the task should expose a weakness of the current agent. Tasks that are already solved reliably provide little new training signal. The useful region is therefore tasks that are feasible and realistic, but not yet consistently solved.
The verifier determines whether the resulting trajectory successfully completes the task. It should satisfy three properties.
Consistency. It should agree with the user prompt, the system specification, and the task-specific environment state.
Soundness. It should reject trajectories that fail to satisfy the task or violate relevant constraints.
Completeness. It should accept valid solutions rather than encode one particular reference trajectory.
These properties matter directly during training. A lax verifier can reward incorrect behavior, while an overly restrictive verifier can penalize valid solutions.

Given an environment and a target model, AutoSynthData generates training tasks consisting of a system specification, user prompt, and verifier. The generated tasks are grounded in the environment and selected to provide useful training signal for the current model.

AutoSynthData first evaluates the target model in the environment using diagnostic tasks and identifies patterns in the tasks it struggles to complete. A stronger teacher helps characterize which of those tasks are solvable and what successful behavior looks like. AutoSynthData turns the resulting capability gaps into new executable tasks, checks each task in the environment, and uses accepted samples for post-training. Evaluating the updated model reveals which gaps remain and can guide the next round of generation.

AutoSynthData uses evaluation runs in the target environment to identify what the model needs to learn next. In our EnterpriseOps Gym experiment, we run both the target model and a stronger teacher on the evaluation tasks. We examine those runs to identify:

We distill these findings into sanitized capability specification cards. The evaluation tasks guide what the model should learn, but the generator does not receive their original prompts, entities, trajectories, or verifier details. It receives the cards and uses them to create new tasks with different prompts, states, and solution paths.
Identifying a capability gap tells us what to teach, but training requires many varied tasks that exercise it. AutoSynthData uses the specification card to generate those tasks.
Suppose the target model struggles with tasks that require the following workflow:

The generator creates new tasks that exercise this workflow, varying the entities, initial environment state, workflow composition, tool combinations, wording, and difficulty. The stronger teacher then demonstrates a successful trajectory for each task. For supervised fine-tuning (SFT), these demonstrations teach the target model how to apply the capability in new situations.
AutoSynthData builds the dataset in two phases: first generating and validating core samples, then expanding them into novel variants.

The target phase creates the core set of training samples from the capability specifications. Workers generate independent tasks in parallel, picking up a new target when they finish. Each candidate goes through validation, execution, solver evaluation, and repair before acceptance. The result is a batch of vetted examples built around what the target model needs to learn.

The multiply phase expands the dataset by creating novel variants of accepted target samples. Each variant has its own user request, environment state, entity configuration, reference trajectory, and verifier, and must pass the same validation and execution checks. A multiplied sample cannot seed another multiplied sample. This anchors expansion to the vetted target set and limits drift across generations.

To support both phases, AutoSynthData separates generation control from environment-specific execution. A shared controller coordinates generation, quality control, coverage, and dataset construction, while an adapter handles environment execution, task and state management, reference replay, deterministic verification, solver execution, and task profiling.

Together, parallel target generation and multiplication provide a path to training-scale datasets. Their usefulness depends on the checks applied to every candidate: the task must be executable, the solution must work, and the verifier must distinguish success from failure.

Generating a plausible request is not enough to produce useful training data. A task may be impossible in the target environment, its reference solution may fail when executed, or its verifier may reward the wrong final state. AutoSynthData checks these properties before accepting a task for training.
AutoSynthData reviews quality at two levels: individual candidates must pass verification, and batches must provide useful coverage and diversity.

Each candidate must clear a quality-control loop before entering the training dataset. We begin with solver evaluation to measure difficulty. In the configuration used here, we favor tasks the target model solves on no more than one of three trials and the stronger solver solves on at least two of three trials. Candidates also undergo positive and negative verification and a bounded repair process.
The positive gate asks: Does the intended solution solve the generated task?

The pipeline executes the reference trajectory in the target environment and checks the resulting state against the candidate’s verifier. This reveals mismatches among the prompt, initial state, solution, and success criteria.
The negative gate asks: Do relevant incorrect outcomes fail?

For example, it can mutate parts of the expected outcome and confirm that those states no longer pass verification. This catches weak verifiers that award success without requiring the intended behavior.

Failed candidates go to a critic before being discarded. The critic examines the sample and its failure, looking for inconsistent state, impossible workflows, incorrect task construction, bad reference trajectories, weak verifier logic, or a mismatch with the intended capability. The critic’s findings guide repairs, with a fixed limit on retries:
A repaired task must pass the relevant checks again. The diagnosis guides repairs to the existing candidate rather than requiring generation to start over.

Passing these checks makes a sample eligible for training, but individually valid samples can still form a repetitive or unbalanced dataset. AutoSynthData therefore also reviews generation at the batch level.
A batch may overrepresent a few easy task families, miss a capability, or reflect too much generation effort spent on a low-yield pattern.
A meta-review examines accepted samples, rejected samples, and generation behavior across each batch. It asks:

The controller tracks coverage in the accepted dataset, reduces generation in overrepresented regions, and directs more work toward gaps. When a region repeatedly produces poor candidates, critiques and meta-review guide changes to the generation strategy. These adjustments balance useful learning signal, task quality, coverage, diversity, and low redundancy within the available generation budget and dataset size requirements.
Together, these feedback loops improve both individual tasks and the dataset they form: sample-level checks guide candidate repair, while batch-level review guides future generation.

The useful training distribution changes as the model improves. AutoSynthData treats synthetic data generation as a search for tasks near the target model's capability boundary: difficult enough to expose weaknesses, but solvable enough for the teacher to provide reliable demonstrations.

After post-training, we evaluate the updated model in the same environment. Tasks it now solves reliably are less useful for the next training round; persistent failures point to capabilities that still need attention. Those results can guide the next generation round.

Our experiments focus on SFT, but the same mechanism could support reinforcement learning (RL): generate tasks that challenge the current policy and provide reliable learning signal, train, then move the generation target with the updated policy. We plan to test this moving, difficulty-calibrated frontier beyond SFT.

We use EnterpriseOps Gym to test whether this approach improves a model on tasks in a stateful enterprise environment. We generate training tasks in the Gym’s Hybrid and ITSM environments, fine-tune the target model on accepted samples, and evaluate the resulting checkpoints.
We tested the pipeline on the Hybrid domain of EnterpriseOps Gym using Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it as the target model and Qwen3.8-27B as the teacher.

AutoSynthData generated 2,000 synthetic training samples in about 18 hours. We fine-tuned Gemma on this dataset and evaluated the resulting checkpoints on the benchmark. The best checkpoint was epoch 5.

The synthetic SFT checkpoint improves mean Pass@1 by 7.2 percentage points, a 35% relative improvement, and raises verifier success from 63.01% to 68.55%. It closes 59% of the original Pass@1 gap between Gemma and the reference model.

The training tasks were newly generated from capability specifications; the generator did not receive the original evaluation tasks. The result demonstrates improvement in EnterpriseOps Gym Hybrid, the environment used for this experiment.

We also applied AutoSynthData to the ITSM domain of EnterpriseOps Gym, using Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it as the target model and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash as the teacher. AutoSynthData generated 1,994 synthetic training samples in 66 hours. Generation took longer than in the subsequent Hybrid run described above, primarily because the ITSM run used a larger teacher model and preceded pipeline optimizations that improved throughput.
On ITSM, synthetic SFT raises mean Pass@1 from 18.77% to 27.18%, showing that the approach also improves performance in a second domain.

The tasks most useful for training depend on both the environment and the model working in it. AutoSynthData uses the model’s failures to choose what to generate, validates new tasks against the environment, and makes those tasks available for post-training. Our EnterpriseOps Gym results show the value of that approach in a controlled setting. As the model changes, the same process can focus on the gaps that remain.

cards.summary_cn: 【Hugging Face 官方动态】AutoSynthData：为企业代理生成训练数据
fulltext_cn: 什么是有用的代理任务？系统规范 面向代理的任务 验证者 概述 从模型失败到课程 生成和扩展任务 目标乘法 实施细节 高质量合成数据需要的不仅仅是生成 样本级验证和修复 批次级审查 推动培训前沿 EnterpriseOps 健身房实验 混合 混合结果 ITSM 闭环
企业需要在自己的环境中运行良好的代理。他们要求这些代理所做的工作是由他们使用的系统、他们遵循的规则以及他们的数据状态决定的。一个模型可能具有广泛的能力，但仍然难以适应特定的环境：它处理不佳的工作流程、它误用的工具组合，或者它未能遵守的约束。这些都是企业需要改进的短板。
困难在于将这些弱点转化为训练数据。个人的失败可以告诉我们一些事情，但是训练模型需要许多新任务，这些任务在不同的情况下发挥相同的能力。这些任务还必须能够在环境中完成，类​​似于某人实际请求的工作，并且有可靠的方法来检查代理是否成功。

在 ServiceNow CoreAI，我们构建了 AutoSynthData，将这些能力差距转化为训练数据。它使用目标模型的失败和更强大的教师的成功来决定模型接下来应该学习什么，然后生成并验证锻炼这些能力的新任务。随着模型的改进，课程转向了它仍然认为困难的部分。我们使用已发布的数据集通过 EnterpriseOps Gym（Malay 等人，2026）说明了管道。我们首先描述代理运行的环境以及任务对训练有用的原因。
代理环境定义了代理操作的世界：它可以观察和修改的状态，它可以调用的工具和 API，以及它的操作产生的状态转换。
任务在此环境中实例化。我们使用以下抽象：
系统规范定义了代理运行的约束，包括系统指令、环境策略，以及适用时特定于任务的初始化，例如种子数据库状态或一组知识文章。
该规范必须与环境的工具、状态和支持的操作兼容。其说明应该清晰，并避免仅仅为了制造难度而引入任意限制。
用户提示指定用户希望代理完成的任务以及任何用户级别的约束。生成的任务应满足三个属性。
可行性。当前环境中应该存在至少一条满足用户提示同时尊重系统规范的轨迹。这排除了依赖于不可用的工具、无法访问的知识、不可能的状态转换或策略禁止的操作的任务。
现实主义。用户提示应该类似于用户在目标环境中可能提出的问题。可执行行为的空间通常比实际工作流的空间大得多。
困难。对于训练，任务应该暴露当前智能体的弱点。已经可靠解决的任务几乎没有提供新的训练信号。因此，有用的区域是可行且现实的任务，但尚未得到一致解决。
验证者确定生成的轨迹是否成功完成任务。它应该满足三个属性。
一致性。它应该与用户提示、系统规范和特定任务的环境状态一致。
健全性。它应该拒绝无法满足任务或违反相关约束的轨迹。
完整性。它应该接受有效的解决方案，而不是编码一个特定的参考轨迹。
这些属性在训练过程中直接重要。宽松的验证者可能会奖励不正确的行为，而过度限制的验证者可能会惩罚有效的解决方案。
给定环境和目标模型，AutoSynthData 生成由系统规范、用户提示和验证器组成的训练任务。生成的任务基于环境并被选择为当前模型提供有用的训练信号。
AutoSynthData 首先使用诊断任务评估环境中的目标模型，并识别其难以完成的任务中的模式。一个更强大的老师可以帮助描述哪些任务是可以解决的以及成功的行为是什么样的。 AutoSynthData 将由此产生的能力差距转化为新的可执行任务，检查环境中的每个任务，并使用接受的样本进行后期训练。评估更新后的模型可以揭示仍然存在哪些差距，并可以指导下一轮的发展。
AutoSynthData 使用目标环境中的评估运行来确定模型接下来需要学习的内容。在我们的 EnterpriseOps Gym 实验中，我们在评估任务上运行目标模型和更强的教师。我们检查这些运行以确定：
我们将这些发现提炼成经过净化的能力规范卡。评估任务指导模型应该学习什么，但生成器不会收到其原始提示、实体、轨迹或验证者详细信息。它接收卡片并使用它们创建具有不同提示、状态和解决方案路径的新任务。
识别能力差距告诉我们要教什么，但培训需要许多不同的任务来锻炼它。 AutoSynthData 使用规范卡来生成这些任务。
假设目标模型难以处理需要以下工作流程的任务：
生成器创建执行此工作流的新任务，改变实体、初始环境状态、工作流组成、工具组合、措辞和难度。然后，能力更强的老师会展示每项任务的成功轨迹。对于监督微调（SFT），这些演示教导目标模型如何在新情况下应用该功能。
AutoSynthData 分两个阶段构建数据集：首先生成和验证核心样本，然后将其扩展为新的变体。
目标阶段根据能力规范创建核心训练样本集。工作人员并行生成独立的任务，完成后选择新的目标。每个候选者在接受之前都要经过验证、执行、求解器评估和修复。结果是围绕目标模型需要学习的内容构建了一批经过审查的示例。
乘法阶段通过创建可接受的目标样本的新变体来扩展数据集。每个变体都有自己的用户请求、环境状态、实体配置、参考轨迹和验证器，并且必须通过相同的验证和执行检查。一个倍增样本不能播种另一个倍增样本。这将扩展锚定在经过审查的目标集上，并限制了代际间的漂移。
为了支持这两个阶段，AutoSynthData 将生成控制与特定于环境的执行分开。共享控制器协调生成、质量控制、覆盖和数据集构建，而适配器处理环境执行、任务和状态管理、参考重放、确定性验证、求解器执行和任务分析。
并行目标生成和乘法共同提供了训练规模数据集的路径。它们的有用性取决于对每个候选者进行的检查：任务必须可执行，解决方案必须有效，验证者必须区分成功与失败。
生成合理的请求不足以产生有用的训练数据。任务在目标环境中可能是不可能的，其参考解决方案在执行时可能会失败，或其验证者可能会奖励错误的最终状态。 AutoSynthData 在接受训练任务之前会检查这些属性。
AutoSynthData 在两个层面上审查质量：单个候选人必须通过验证，批次必须提供有用的覆盖范围和多样性。
每个候选人在进入训练数据集之前都必须清除质量控制循环。我们从求解器评估开始来衡量难度。在此处使用的配置中，我们倾向于目标模型在不超过三个试验中的一个上解决任务，而更强的求解器在三个试验中的至少两个上解决。候选者还要接受正面和负面验证以及有界修复过程。
正门问：预期的解决方案是否解决了生成的任务？
管道在目标环境中执行参考轨迹，并根据候选验证者检查结果状态。这揭示了提示、初始状态、解决方案和成功标准之间的不匹配。
负门问：相关的错误结果会失败吗？
例如，它可以改变部分预期结果并确认这些状态不再通过验证。这会捕获那些在不需要预期行为的情况下授予成功的弱验证者。
失败的候选人在被抛弃之前会去找批评家。批评者检查样本及其失败，寻找不一致的状态、不可能的工作流程、不正确的任务构造、错误的参考轨迹、薄弱的验证者逻辑或与预期功能的不匹配。批评者的发现指导了修复，对重试有固定的限制：
修复后的任务必须再次通过相关检查。诊断指导对现有候选者的修复，而不是要求发电重新开始。
通过这些检查使样本符合训练条件，但单独有效的样本仍然可以形成重复或不平衡的数据集。因此，AutoSynthData 还会在批次级别审查生成。
一个批次可能会过度代表一些简单的任务系列，错过某个功能，或者反映出在低产量模式上花费了太多的生成努力。
元审查检查接受的样本、拒绝的样本以及每个批次的生成行为。它问：
控制器跟踪已接受数据集中的覆盖范围，减少代表性过高区域的生成，并将更多工作引导到空白区域。当一个地区反复产生糟糕的候选人时，批评和元审查会引导对生成策略的改变。这些调整在可用的生成预算和数据集大小要求内平衡有用的学习信号、任务质量、覆盖范围、多样性和低冗余。
这些反馈循环共同改善了单个任务及其形成的数据集：样本级检查指导候选修复，而批次级审查指导下一代。
有用的训练分布随着模型的改进而变化。 AutoSynthData 将合成数据生成视为对目标模型能力边界附近任务的搜索：困难到足以暴露弱点，但又足够容易解决，以便教师提供可靠的演示。
训练后，我们在相同的环境中评估更新后的模型。它现在可靠解决的任务对于下一轮训练来说用处不大；持续的故障表明仍然需要关注的功能。这些结果可以指导下一代回合。
我们的实验侧重于 SFT，但相同的机制可以支持强化学习（RL）：生成挑战当前策略的任务并提供可靠的学习信号，训练，然后用更新的策略移动生成目标。我们计划在 SFT 之外测试这个移动的、难度校准的前沿。
我们使用 EnterpriseOps Gym 来测试这种方法是否改进了有状态企业环境中的任务模型。我们在 Gym 的混合和 ITSM 环境中生成训练任务，在接受的样本上微调目标模型，并评估生成的检查点。
我们使用 Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it 作为目标模型，Qwen3.8-27B 作为教师，在 EnterpriseOps Gym 的混合域上测试了管道。
AutoSynthData 在大约 18 小时内生成了 2,000 个合成训练样本。我们在此数据集上对 Gemma 进行了微调，并在基准测试中评估了生成的检查点。最好的检查点是 epoch 5。
合成 SFT 检查点将平均 Pass@1 提高了 7.2 个百分点，相对提高了 35%，并将验证者的成功率从 63.01% 提高到 68.55%。它缩小了 Gemma 与参考模型之间 59% 的原始 Pass@1 差距。
训练任务是根据能力规范新生成的；生成器没有收到原来的评估任务。结果证明了用于本实验的环境 EnterpriseOps Gym Hybrid 的改进。

我们还将 AutoSynthData 应用到 EnterpriseOps Gym 的 ITSM 域中，使用 Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it 作为目标模型，使用 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 作为教师。 AutoSynthData 在 66 小时内生成了 1,994 个合成训练样本。生成时间比上述随后的混合运行要长，主要是因为 ITSM 运行使用了更大的教师模型，并且在管道优化之前提高了吞吐量。
在 ITSM 上，合成 SFT 将平均 Pass@1 从 18.77% 提高到 27.18%，表明该方法还提高了第二个域的性能。
对训练最有用的任务取决于环境和在其中运行的模型。 AutoSynthData 使用模型的失败来选择要生成的内容，根据环境验证新任务，并使这些任务可用于后期训练。我们的 EnterpriseOps Gym 结果显示了该方法在受控环境中的价值。随着模型的变化，相同的过程可以专注于仍然存在的差距。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 2 日消息，当地时间 9 月 30 日晚，OpenAI 披露，旗下 AI 智能体或曾擅自尝试绕过安全防护，或对百余家机构的系统造成负面影响。
OpenAI 此次披露的信息显示，已知的 AI 智能体失控行为涉及范围进一步扩大。公司已向 100 多家第三方机构发出通知，告知这些机构发现了“智能体偏离预期的行为”。

IT之家获悉，具体情况包括 AI 智能体试图让网站执行非预期命令、把网站当作共享留言板使用，以及绕过某些安全检查。
OpenAI 强调，收到通知并不代表系统一定遭到入侵。这些活动更接近于试探一扇上锁的门，而非真正破门而入。
OpenAI 表示，公司希望向受影响的第三方提供必要信息，以便调查和处理潜在的安全或其他技术问题。OpenAI 还承诺公开分享对模型行为、安全防护中新型薄弱环节的研究结果，帮助更广泛的 AI 和安全研究界改进安全工作。
OpenAI 披露这些情况前，独立研究人员发现了一系列涉及失控 AI 智能体的网络安全事件。《华盛顿邮报》曾报道，行为方式与 OpenAI 系统相似的 AI 智能体曾试图入侵加拿大政府网站。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 2 日消息，据央视新闻报道，国庆假期第一天（10 月 1 日），新能源车辆预计达 1780 万辆次。交通运输部提示，重点高速、通往热门景区的服务区车流大，充电需求相对集中，尤其是每天 10 时以后。
今年国庆长假，出行总量大、范围广，拥堵缓行路段呈多点分布，拥堵程度预计增强。旅游流成为假期出行主力，杭州、西安、长沙等城市景区附近公路，可能出现流量较多情况；新疆、青海、甘肃等长线游热门省份，也会出现局部阶段性交通压力增大情况。
为了应对假期期间新能源车辆充电的需求，交通运输部提前根据历年车联网平台数据进行研判分析，在中秋国庆假期前就建立了充电特别繁忙服务区清单，在这些服务区通过增加移动充电设备、大功率快充设备等缓解充电需求。
国庆假期，全国充电特别繁忙的高速服务区有：
秦滨高速河北段乐亭服务区、唐海服务区；
连霍高速江苏段彭城服务区；
沈海高速福建段云淡停车区；
沙厦高速福建段秀村服务区；
京港澳高速河南段漯河服务区；
菏宝高速河南段王屋山服务区；
长芷高速湖南段桥头河服务区；
京昆高速四川段新安服务区；
京昆高速陕西段澄城服务区。
交通运输部提醒，新能源车主还可通过“e 路畅通”微信小程序，一键查询充电服务；如果在路上遇到了需要救援的情况，也可以一键呼叫救援。
IT之家从报道获悉，根据交通运输部的预测，国庆假期新能源出行车辆较多，日均车辆是日常新能源车出行的 1.8 倍，高速公路充电需求整体呈现“出程分散、回程集中”的特点。
每天从 10 时开始，高速公路服务区充电场站车辆开始显著增加，21 时后车流逐步回落，充电需求随之减少。
10 月 5 日和 6 日是返程核心时段，高速公路充电车辆将大幅增加。充电高峰时段为 10 月 5 日的 11 时至 21 时，10 月 6 日的 10 时至 22 时。

cards.title: OpenAI’s new agent is a shot at Meta — but can it compete with free?
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 的新代理是对 Meta 的一次尝试——但它能与免费代理竞争吗？
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】At OpenAI's annual DevDay conference, the company pulled out all the stops to compete with its rivals - primarily Meta, whose Muse AI agent platform has seen early runaway success. CEO Sam Altman walk…
fulltext: OpenAI and Meta’s cutesy AI agents are about to fight to the death.

At OpenAI’s annual DevDay conference, the company pulled out all the stops to compete with its rivals — primarily Meta, whose Muse AI agent platform has seen early runaway success. CEO Sam Altman walked onstage to cheers and announced Dots, a “real-deal AI” agent powered by GPT-6 Astra, “inspired by the cool agents that we all watched in movies growing up.” Similar to Muse, Dots aims for disarming cuteness, taking the form of colorful, personalizable blobs with eyes. OpenAI fired shots at Meta by demonstrating Dots’ ability to not just act as helpful assistants but build metaverse-esque virtual worlds. But in one key area, Dots strikingly fails to compete: price.

Muse’s main selling point is making AI agent access free and frictionless. The company offers a free dedicated virtual machine that houses both the agent and the user’s associated data. OpenAI’s Dots, by contrast, is restricted for now to users on its $100/month Pro plan and up. While anyone with a Meta account can get Muse, most of ChatGPT’s 1.2 billion users won’t be able to use Dots.

There’s an obvious reason for this: OpenAI likely can’t afford it. The AI lab is reportedly currently aiming to raise $30 billion in funding at a $1.4 trillion valuation, per Bloomberg, and it’s experienced 70 percent growth since the beginning of its third quarter — nearing $70 billion in annual recurring revenue, Axios reported. Yet despite its staggering financing, its funds aren’t limitless, particularly compared to a tech giant like Meta. In the past year, some users have accused AI labs of passing costs on to customers amid an AI money squeeze. OpenAI in particular is burning through a lot of cash right now — it expects to spend $280 billion by 2030, per the FT — and compute is expensive, while it’s also facing pressure from investors to button up its bottom line ahead of going public.

“Dots are starting out as a premium product — it uses a lot of compute,” Altman said Tuesday during a private press Q&A after his DevDay keynote, adding, “I think it will help us understand and help people understand how expansive and what AI can do. But you should of course expect us to do a mass-market thing for billions of people someday.”

During DevDay, OpenAI took pains to explain why Dots (with singular agents referred to as a “Dot”) are worth the money, positioning it as not just a capable personal assistant but a “chief of staff” or experienced engineer. OpenAI employee Holly Li told the audience using a Dot was “like talking to a second brain.” Altman said that Dots were built for delegating “ambitious pieces of work,” like QA for an unreleased product, website design, team offsite trip planning, portfolio rebalancing, and email campaign creation. “Specialist” Dots, trained for areas like accounting and legal analysis, are supposed to launch soon, and the company is working with Microsoft to integrate them into its Agent 365 platform.
The goal, Altman said, is to go beyond agents that simply book reservations, purchase meals, search calendars, and schedule appointments — classic use cases for consumer-facing tools like Muse.

When asked during the press Q&A how Dots is different from Muse and Instinct, another popular new AI agent, Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI’s head of core products, said it’s “capable of actually staying on track in very long periods of time.” He added that the multimodality of Dots, which will allow chatting with an agent via text or voice mode and phone call, will feel like “an incredible extension of you.” (The voice demos of Dots didn’t work at DevDay, though, and though OpenAI leaders highlighted the texting-your-agent feature multiple times at the conference, that feature — already supported by Muse and Instinct — is still slated as coming soon.)

Altman said during the Q&A that the long-horizon and knowledge-work tasks were what set Dots apart, adding, “I think this is far beyond anything else available on the market today.” He said that the agents’ help with triaging to-do lists and supporting employees at work would be “difficult for economists to measure right away” but would hopefully make a “huge difference” in how people feel about their jobs.

Framing Dots as a professional tool not only differentiates Dots from Muse, but could help OpenAI gain ground against Anthropic in the enterprise market. Anthropic has focused on — and dominated in — enterprise AI for years, but OpenAI has devoted more resources to the area over the past year. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC that the company’s enterprise business had doubled since July.

OpenAI leads also tried to promote Dots as safer and more secure, particularly compared to Muse. Alexander Embiricos, the company’s Codex product lead, said OpenAI is focused on having the “most trustworthy, safe, and secure assistant,” highlighting that it’s powered by GPT-6 Astra, the company’s “most aligned model.” During the DevDay keynote, executives also presented “OpenAI Private Intelligence,” a data privacy framework that allows businesses to have “stronger controls” over their data, as well as zero data retention policy options, with no data stored on OpenAI servers.

Altman said onstage that OpenAI hopes to “set a new standard for privacy in frontier AI.” The comments come after Muse was recently lambasted for taking over a user’s Facebook Marketplace account and giving out their address to a stranger without the user realizing.

“I think we’re in a different position to Meta in that they don’t have an AI product that has 1.2 billion users,” Glen Coates, OpenAI’s head of app platform, told The Verge in an interview. “Launching something that makes those kinds of mistakes is something that we would try to take the care to avoid. I think we’re trying to be really deliberate with how we let our agents use plug-ins, how we let agents use your identity and sign-in/sign up for things, how we let your agents pay for things.”

The question is whether all that is enough to beat free. ChatGPT rose to prominence not only by being first but also by being free — and easy to use even without signing in. Muse may be able to dominate in the AI agent space for the same reason. The other hurdle for making these AI agents as frictionless as possible is that Meta offers easy integration with the other platforms it owns, such as Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. (Google’s Gemini Spark agent platform has an advantage for the same reason.) Though OpenAI said users would be able to connect Dots to a wide range of external tools, they may not be as seamless as an in-house integration.

For now, OpenAI is hoping that a better product will trump a cheaper one. “We might move a tiny bit slower, but we also know that if people have Dots that go out there and YOLO-buy stuff on Facebook Marketplace, that’s just not something we want to put 1.2 billion users through,” Coates said. “We’re trying to do it right, basically.”

fulltext_cn: OpenAI 和 Meta 可爱的 AI 代理即将展开殊死搏斗。

在 OpenAI 的年度 DevDay 大会上，该公司使出浑身解数与竞争对手竞争——主要是 Meta，其 Muse AI 代理平台已经取得了早期的巨大成功。首席执行官 Sam Altman 走上台欢呼雀跃，并宣布 Dots 是一款由 GPT-6 Astra 提供支持的“真正的人工智能”代理，“其灵感来自于我们在成长过程中在电影中看到的酷炫代理。”与 Muse 类似，Dots 的目标是消除可爱感，采用色彩缤纷、个性化的眼睛斑点的形式。 OpenAI 向 Meta 发起了攻击，展示了 Dots 不仅能够充当有用的助手，还能构建虚拟世界式的虚拟世界。但在一个关键领域，Dots 明显无法竞争：价格。
Muse 的主要卖点是让人工智能代理能够自由、无摩擦地访问。该公司提供免费的专用虚拟机，其中包含代理和用户的相关数据。相比之下，OpenAI 的 Dots 目前仅限其 100 美元/月 Pro 套餐及以上的用户使用。虽然任何拥有 Meta 帐户的人都可以获得 Muse，但 ChatGPT 的 12 亿用户中的大多数将无法使用 Dots。

这有一个明显的原因：OpenAI 可能负担不起。据彭博社报道，该人工智能实验室目前的目标是筹集 300 亿美元资金，估值为 1.4 万亿美元，据 Axios 报道，自第三季度初以来，该实验室实现了 70% 的增长，年度经常性收入接近 700 亿美元。然而，尽管其融资规模惊人，但其资金并非无限，特别是与 Meta 这样的科技巨头相比。去年，一些用户指责人工智能实验室在人工智能资金紧张的情况下将成本转嫁给客户。尤其是 OpenAI 目前正在消耗大量现金——据英国《金融时报》报道，到 2030 年，它预计将花费 2800 亿美元——而且计算成本昂贵，同时它还面临着投资者在上市前压低盈利的压力。
“Dots 最初是一种高端产品，它使用大量计算，”Altman 周二在 DevDay 主题演讲后的私人媒体问答中说道，并补充道，“我认为这将帮助我们理解并帮助人们了解人工智能的范围和功能。但你当然应该期待我们有一天能为数十亿人做一件面向大众市场的事情。”

在 DevDay 期间，OpenAI 煞费苦心地解释了为什么 Dots（单个代理被称为“Dot”）物有所值，将其定位为不仅是一个有能力的个人助理，而且是一个“参谋长”或经验丰富的工程师。 OpenAI 员工 Holly Li 告诉观众，使用 Dot“就像与第二个大脑交谈”。 Altman 表示，Dots 是为了委派“雄心勃勃的工作”而构建的，例如未发布产品的质量检查、网站设计、团队异地旅行计划、投资组合重新平衡和电子邮件营销活动创建。经过会计和法律分析等领域培训的“专家”Dots 预计很快就会推出，该公司正在与微软合作，将其集成到 Agent 365 平台中。
Altman 表示，我们的目标是超越简单的预订、购买餐食、搜索日历和安排预约的代理——Muse 等面向消费者的工具的经典用例。

当在新闻问答中被问及 Dots 与 Muse 和 Instinct 有何不同时，另一款受欢迎的新 AI 代理 OpenAI 核心产品负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 表示，它“能够在很长一段时间内保持在正轨上”。他补充说，Dots 的多模态功能允许通过文本或语音模式以及电话与客服人员聊天，感觉就像“你的不可思议的延伸”。 （不过，Dots 的语音演示在 DevDay 上并没有发挥作用，尽管 OpenAI 领导者在会议上多次强调了向您的代理发送短信的功能，但该功能（已经得到 Muse 和 Instinct 的支持）仍预计很快就会推出。）
Altman 在问答中表示，长期和知识工作任务是 Dots 的与众不同之处，并补充道，“我认为这远远超出了当今市场上的任何其他产品。”他表示，代理人在分类待办事项清单和支持员工工作方面的帮助“经济学家很难立即衡量”，但有望对人们对工作的看法产生“巨大影响”。
Framing Dots 作为一款专业工具，不仅可以将 Dots 与 Muse 区分开来，还可以帮助 OpenAI 在企业市场上战胜 Anthropic。 Anthropic 多年来一直专注于并在企业人工智能领域占据主导地位，但 OpenAI 在过去一年中向该领域投入了更多资源。 OpenAI 首席财务官 Sarah Friar 告诉 CNBC，自 7 月份以来，该公司的企业业务增长了一倍。

OpenAI 的领导者还试图宣传 Dots 更安全，尤其是与 Muse 相比。该公司 Codex 产品负责人 Alexander Embiricos 表示，OpenAI 专注于拥有“最值得信赖、最安全的助手”，并强调它由该公司“最一致的模型”GPT-6 Astra 提供支持。在 DevDay 主题演讲中，高管们还介绍了“OpenAI Private Intelligence”，这是一个数据隐私框架，允许企业对其数据进行“更强的控制”，以及零数据保留策略选项，并且 OpenAI 服务器上不存储任何数据。
Altman 在台上表示，OpenAI 希望“为前沿人工智能领域的隐私制定新标准”。此前，Muse 最近因接管用户的 Facebook Marketplace 帐户并在用户不知情的情况下将其地址泄露给陌生人而受到严厉批评。
OpenAI 应用平台负责人 Glen Coates 在接受 The Verge 采访时表示：“我认为我们与 Meta 的处境不同，他们没有拥有 12 亿用户的人工智能产品。” “推出会犯此类错误的产品是我们会尽力避免的事情。我认为我们正在努力认真考虑如何让我们的代理使用插件，我们如何让代理使用您的身份并登录/注册事物，我们如何让您的代理为事物付费。”

问题是这一切是否足以击败自由。 ChatGPT 的崛起不仅是因为它是第一，而且因为它是免费的，而且即使没有登录也很容易使用。出于同样的原因，Muse 可能能够在人工智能代理领域占据主导地位。让这些人工智能代理尽可能无摩擦的另一个障碍是 Meta 可以轻松地与其拥有的其他平台集成，例如 Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp。 （出于同样的原因，谷歌的 Gemini Spark 代理平台也具有优势。）尽管 OpenAI 表示用户将能够将 Dots 连接到各种外部工具，但它们可能不如内部集成那么无缝。
目前，OpenAI 希望更好的产品能够胜过更便宜的产品。 “我们的进展可能会慢一点，但我们也知道，如果人们使用 Dots 并在 Facebook Marketplace 上购买 YOLO 商品，那我们就不想让 12 亿用户通过这种方式进行购买，”Coates 说。 “基本上，我们正在努力把事情做好。”

In December 2025, about a month before the U.S. invaded Venezuela and captured its president, Nicolás Maduro, President Trump had a secret meeting with Elon Musk, Time magazine reports. This was roughly seven months after Musk left his role in the Trump administration at the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).

During this meeting, Trump “spent hours” talking to Musk’s Grok chatbot, including asking how Venezuelans would respond to the capture of their president, a source told Time. Just a few months earlier, in September, Trump began ordering U.S. military strikes against Venezuelan boats that Trump alleged were involved in drug trafficking.

People had apparently been turning to Grok asking about the boat strikes and political climate in Venezuela, as The Atlantic reported at the time. So Grok told Trump that Maduro was a “deeply unpopular dictator and that many Venezuelans would likely celebrate his downfall,” Time reported.
When such celebrations indeed happened after the U.S. invaded on January 3, Trump apparently “came away thinking Grok was ingenious,” that source told Time.
So perhaps it should come as no surprise that in June of this year, the Pentagon’s head of AI said that the military used Gov Grok to deploy and strike targets during the Iran War.

While Grok isn’t the only AI model serving the DoD (OpenAI also has an agreement and Anthropic has been in a back-and-forth over how its models can be used for military intelligence and in modern warfare), Grok may become an even bigger favorite under this administration. Earlier this week, the Pentagon announced that Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey have been tapped to co-lead a study about how advanced technology is, and can be, used in battlefields.

OpenAI is again experimenting with how its conversational AI assistant, ChatGPT, can help users as they shop online. On Thursday, the company announced the global launch of two new shopping features, including a way to virtually try on clothing and accessories and a new favoriting function that can help users save products they like for later reference.

The updates arrive at a time when AI assistants are exploring consumer use cases around shopping. OpenAI already had to pivot from one of its earlier ideas in this space, an instant checkout feature that ended up not performing well. More recently, agentic AI startup Instinct began pushing product recommendations to users, but some felt that the proactive recommendations were an overreach, more akin to ads than helpful suggestions.

OpenAI said its new shopping features leverage the newly launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 model, which the company claims produces more natural lighting and richer textures, follows editing instructions more reliably, and reduces image generation latency.

To start, virtual try-on allows ChatGPT users to upload a selfie or a full-body photo in order to visualize how an article of clothing or an accessory might look on them. This option will appear as a new Try On button in ChatGPT’s shopping results. You can also upload an image of an item, like a web screenshot, and ask ChatGPT to try it on for you.

The other new option, Favorites, lets you save products you discover to a Library in the app so you can come back to them later. (These items will be saved alongside your try-on images, the company notes.)
OpenAI said that ChatGPT can help users shop in other ways, too.

For instance, you could describe a style that you’d like to try, then ask it to shop for the pieces needed to complete the look. Or, you could upload photos of celebrities’ outfits and ask it to find the items they’re wearing that are available for purchase.

The latter sees the assistant moving into areas that Pinterest and Google have dominated in recent years as sources for fashion inspiration and discovery that can convert to sales for online retailers.
Whether ChatGPT will become people’s first choice for this type of activity, however, remains to be seen — especially given that Google launched virtual try-on last year.

Now that LLM-generated prose is everywhere, human beings are eager for ways to sniff it out. While early tells like em-dashes and “delve” are long gone, researchers say there are still plenty of telltale habits that AI models fall back on when writing prose.

A new study from the marketing firm Graphite looked at the writing habits of frontier models, sussing out each model’s favorite words and phrases. While old tells like em-dash use have been stamped out, models still fall back on contrast-heavy constructions, with each model version showing its own unique quirks. The biggest surprise is how broad the scope of tells turns out to be. Graphite found 13,000 phrases that were at least twice as common in the AI content as human content — their definition of a “tell.”

“It turns out that Claude models are actually getting closer to the human word distribution over time,” Graphite’s chief AI officer Greg Druck told TechCrunch. “And for the GPT models, it’s getting further away.”

Studying AI-generated writing at scale required a careful study design. Graphite started with a corpus of 10,000 articles published before the release of ChatGPT, serving as the human-generated control group. Then researchers had different AI models rewrite the articles from summaries, hoping to eliminate as much source bias as possible. With matching samples from both humans and each model, they could compare how often certain words and phrases appeared in AI writing, as well as broader patterns in sentence construction.

According to Graphite’s results, Claude Opus 5.5’s biggest tell is the word “dependable,” which pops up 23 times more often than in human samples. While Opus 5.5 now avoids the “it’s not X, it’s Y” sentence construction, it still tends to say something “is more than an X, it’s a Y.”
Above all, Opus loves to tell you why things matter, using the phrase “this matters” 116 times more often than human writing, while “why X matters” occurs 92 times more often.

OpenAI’s Astra has a different set of tip-offs. This model loves to describe “another dimension” of whatever it’s talking about, and tends to hedge claims by saying an action “may provide” or “can provide” a particular benefit. Its biggest tell is what Graphite calls the “corrective framing,” where a topic is defined as “not simply X” or offered as an alternative, “rather than relying on X.” According to graphite’s research, those constructions were more than 100 times more common in Astra-generated prose than in human writing.

Notably, all the frontier labs seem to have responded to the idea that models overuse em-dashes. In Graphite’s samples, Opus 5.5 used the punctuation mark 99% less often than Opus 5. Astra now uses it 88% less than human samples, whereas Gemini 3.1 Pro has almost completely eliminated the em-dash from its writing.

But while individual tells change, Graphite says the overall number is mostly holding steady. “It’s not like the tells are decreasing,” Druck told TechCrunch. “They are managing to remove the most well-known tells, but other ones pop up. And every model version has its own.”

It’s surprising that tells are so persistent, given the labs’ focus on human-like writing styles. In the Opus 5.5 release, Anthropic boasted that the model “communicates more naturally than prior models,” saying early users “found its writing clearer and easier to follow.”
OpenAI made similar claims when releasing the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna, saying users could “expect to see more clarity, less jargon, [and] fewer odd turns of phrase.”
But Druck is skeptical about how much the labs can do to completely eliminate telltale construction or phrases.

“A general hypothesis I have is that the labs are less able to control some of these things than you might expect,” Druck says. “These are giant models with billions of parameters. They have some finite number of tests they can run, and things slip through.”

现在法学硕士生成的散文无处不在，人们渴望找到方法来嗅出它。虽然像破折号和“深入研究”这样的早期讲述方式早已不复存在，但研究人员表示，人工智能模型在撰写散文时仍然依赖很多讲述习惯。
营销公司 Graphite 的一项新研究着眼于前沿模特的写作习惯，找出每个模特最喜欢的单词和短语。虽然像破折号这样的旧说法已经被淘汰，但模型仍然依赖于对比强烈的结构，每个模型版本都显示出自己独特的怪癖。最大的惊喜是讲述的范围有多么广泛。 Graphite 发现了 13,000 个短语，这些短语在人工智能内容中的出现频率至少是人类内容的两倍——他们对“告诉”的定义。
“事实证明，随着时间的推移，Claude 模型实际上越来越接近人类的单词分布，”Graphite 首席人工智能官 Greg Druck 告诉 TechCrunch。 “而对于 GPT 模型来说，它已经越来越远了。”
大规模研究人工智能生成的写作需要仔细的研究设计。 Graphite 从 ChatGPT 发布之前发布的 10,000 篇文章的语料库开始，作为人类生成的对照组。然后研究人员让不同的人工智能模型根据摘要重写文章，希望尽可能消除来源偏见。通过匹配人类和每个模型的样本，他们可以比较某些单词和短语在人工智能写作中出现的频率，以及句子结构中更广泛的模式。
根据 Graphite 的结果，Claude Opus 5.5 最大的亮点是“可靠”这个词，它出现的频率是人类样本的 23 倍。虽然 Opus 5.5 现在避免了“这不是 X，这是 Y”的句子结构，但它仍然倾向于说“这不仅仅是 X，这是 Y”。
最重要的是，Opus 喜欢告诉您为什么事情很重要，“这很重要”这个短语的使用频率比人类书写的频率高 116 倍，而“为什么 X 很重要”的出现频率是人类书写的 92 倍。

OpenAI 的 Astra 有一组不同的提示。这个模型喜欢描述它所谈论的任何事物的“另一个维度”，并且倾向于通过说某个行为“可能提供”或“可以提供”特定的好处来对冲主张。它最大的亮点是 Graphite 所说的“纠正框架”，其中一个主题被定义为“不仅仅是 X”或作为替代方案提供，“而不是依赖 X”。根据 Graphite 的研究，这些结构在 Astra 生成的散文中比在人类写作中常见 100 倍以上。
值得注意的是，所有前沿实验室似乎都对模型过度使用破折号的想法做出了回应。在 Graphite 的样本中，Opus 5.5 使用标点符号的频率比 Opus 5 少 99%。Astra 现在使用标点符号的频率比人类样本少 88%，而 Gemini 3.1 Pro 几乎完全消除了书写中的破折号。
尽管个人表示有所变化，但 Graphite 表示总体数字基本保持稳定。 “这并不是说信息正在减少，”德鲁克告诉 TechCrunch。 “他们设法删除了最知名的内容，但其他内容又出现了。而且每个模型版本都有自己的版本。”
令人惊讶的是，鉴于实验室专注于类人写作风格，讲述如此持久。在 Opus 5.5 版本中，Anthropic 吹嘘该模型“比以前的模型沟通更自然”，并表示早期用户“发现它的文字更清晰、更容易理解”。
OpenAI 在发布 Sol 和 Luna 的 GPT-6 版本时也做出了类似的声明，称用户可以“期望看到更清晰、更少的行话和更少的奇怪短语”。
但德鲁克对实验室能在多大程度上完全消除泄露线索的结构或短语持怀疑态度。
“我的一个普遍假设是，实验室控制其中一些事情的能力比你想象的要低，”德鲁克说。 “这些是具有数十亿个参数的巨型模型。它们可以运行的测试数量有限，但事情却会被忽略。”
